content.text: The Mistake Almost Every Creator Makes First: Ebooks nigeria

The biggest mistake creators make when selling ebooks in Nigeria without PayPal is relying on alternative payment processors like Stripe, which may not be available in their country or can be shut down at any time. This is because Stripe operates in only 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving a significant gap in coverage. Moreover, once a creator is shut out by Stripe, they may not be able to recover their funds, which can take up to 180 days with no appeal. This is a ticking time bomb for creators who rely on these platforms for their livelihood.
Why This Keeps Happening Even to Experienced Sellers

Experienced sellers fall into this trap because they often underestimate the risks associated with relying on third-party payment processors. They may think that Stripe or PayPal is a safe and reliable option, but the reality is that these platforms can be shut down or restricted at any time, leaving creators in a precarious position. This is especially true for creators in countries with restrictive financial regulations or those that are not supported by these platforms. In Nigeria, for example, many creators have been affected by PayPal's country restrictions, which have made it difficult for them to receive payments from customers.
The Real Cost of Getting This Wrong

The real cost of getting this wrong is not just financial, but also reputational and emotional. When a creator's payment processor is shut down, they may lose not only their income but also their customers' trust. This can have a long-term impact on their business, making it difficult to recover from the loss. Moreover, the emotional toll of dealing with a platform shutdown can be significant, causing stress, anxiety, and even burnout. This is why it's essential for creators to take control of their infrastructure and build a stack that cannot be taken down.

With this stack, creators can collect payments from customers directly, manage their data securely, and maintain control over their business.
